title: Stream JSON log viewer with filtered views for AI agent output
description:
Add a frontend log display mode for jobs that produce Claude CLI stream-json output (--output-format stream-json). The raw log is NDJSON with multiple event types:

- type: system (init metadata — session_id, tools, model, etc.)
- type: assistant with content[].type: text (AI agent's thinking/response text)
- type: assistant with content[].type: tool_use (tool calls — name, input params)
- type: user with content[].type: tool_result (tool call results)
- type: result (final summary — success/error, cost, usage stats)

The viewer should support filter modes:
1. RAW — current behavior, show full log as-is
2. MESSAGES — show only the AI's text responses (assistant events where content contains type: text). Strip the JSON wrapper and display the text field directly. This gives a clean conversation view.
3. TOOL CALLS — show assistant tool_use events as expandable cards (tool name as header, input params collapsed by default). Optionally pair with the corresponding tool_result.
4. ALL PARSED — show all events in a structured timeline with type badges, expandable JSON details

Detection: auto-detect stream-json format by checking if the first line of the log parses as JSON with a type field. If detected, offer the filter toggle. If not, fall back to raw display.

Example data structure from a real run is documented in the ticket discussion.

title: Configurable per-job concurrency — allow multiple simultaneous instances
description:
## Problem

Currently, the `active_runs` HashMap in the daemon is keyed by `job_id`, meaning only one instance of a job can run at a time. If a job's schedule fires while a previous run is still active, the old RunHandle is silently overwritten, potentially orphaning the previous run (which may appear as Killed).

This is a blocker for multi-tenant use cases such as AI chat/agent systems where the same job definition (e.g. an 'agent' job) needs to serve multiple tenants simultaneously.

## Proposed Solution

Add a per-job boolean field `allow_concurrent` (default: `false`) that controls whether multiple simultaneous runs of a single job are permitted.

### Current Behavior (keep as-is when allow_concurrent = false)
- Only one run per job at a time
- If a new run starts while one is active, the previous run is killed
- This is the existing behavior and remains the default

### New Behavior (when allow_concurrent = true)
- Multiple runs of the same job can execute simultaneously with no cap
- Change `active_runs` from `HashMap<Uuid, RunHandle>` (keyed by job_id) to support multiple runs per job (e.g. keyed by run_id, or `HashMap<Uuid, Vec<RunHandle>>`)
- Ensure kill/shutdown logic handles multiple active runs per job
- Update API endpoints (create/update job) to accept the new field

### Out of Scope
- Capping the number of concurrent instances (no max_instances limit)
- Changing the kill-on-overlap behavior for non-concurrent jobs

### Frontend Changes
- Add `allow_concurrent` toggle/checkbox to the job creation/edit form
- Default: off (false)

## Use Case

AI agent/chat systems where a single job definition (the 'agent') is shared across multiple tenants who may trigger it concurrently.

title: Auto-add ACS binary to user PATH on install/start
description: When the ACS daemon is installed or started for the first time, it should automatically add its binary location to the user-level PATH environment variable so that 'acs' can be called from any terminal without requiring the user to manually configure their PATH. This should use user-level PATH modification (not system-level) to avoid requiring elevated permissions. Platform-specific approaches: Windows - modify HKCU\Environment\Path registry key; macOS/Linux - append to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, or ~/.profile.
close_reason: Implemented: renamed binary from acs to agentcronsystem across all platforms. Added automatic PATH modification on install/start for Windows (registry), macOS (zshrc/bash_profile), and Linux (bashrc/zshrc/profile). Updated all service identifiers, Electron packaging, CI workflows, tests, and documentation.

comments.author: Jacob Tonna
comments.text: Scope update: Rename binary from 'acs' to 'agentcronsystem' before adding to PATH. Research found naming conflicts — Qualcomm Atheros acs.exe exists in Windows System32 (common on laptops), and Splunk has an actively maintained CLI also called 'acs'. Renaming avoids collisions on all platforms.

title: Electron frontend uses static export requiring manual route registration — switch to standalone mode
description: The Electron frontend uses Next.js output: export which requires every dynamic route to declare generateStaticParams manually. This causes routes like /jobs/new (now /jobs/create) to fail in the compiled Electron build because the client-side router does not resolve them correctly. Dev mode works fine. Fix: switch from output: export to output: standalone so Next.js produces a self-contained Node.js server. Electron already has Node.js built in, so the standalone server can run directly. This eliminates generateStaticParams, the custom static file server, the tryDynamicRoute hack, and the _ placeholder pattern entirely.
close_reason: Fixed: switched Electron frontend from Next.js static export to standalone mode. Eliminates generateStaticParams, custom static file server, and tryDynamicRoute hack. All routes now work automatically.

title: Job lifecycle hooks — before, during, and after execution
description: Research and design a hooks system for ACS jobs. Three hook types: pre-execution (before job starts — validate preconditions, acquire locks), during-execution (monitor live output, pattern matching, interactive stdin), post-execution (cleanup, notifications, job chaining). Key questions: what form do hooks take (shell commands, other ACS jobs, plugins)? Per-job vs global config? Failure propagation? Interaction with PTY/SSE streaming? Relationship to ENH-002 output parsing? Expected output: design document, data model changes, API surface, complexity estimate.
